movesets.name: Poison Heal
movesets.description:
Set Details

Breloom's unique defensive profile makes it a great check to the tier's Dark-types like Krookodile, Umbreon, and Wo-Chien as well as Rhyperior, and it's a decent wallbreaker with good resilience. It's also able to switch into the many Scalds and Thunder Waves in the tier after it activates Poison Heal. In addition, status-boosted Facade allows Breloom to damage Flying- and Poison-type Pokemon such as Noivern and Amoonguss. Protect scouts the intention of Choice-locked Pokemon, like Galarian Zapdos and Basculegion-F, while also racking up Poison Heal recovery. Protect also ensures Toxic Orb is activated when Breloom first enters the field. 176 Speed EVs allow Breloom to outspeed Modest offensive Empoleon and Hisuian Goodra. Maximum HP allows Breloom to stomach hits such as Psychic Noise from Jirachi and Slowbro, allowing it to outlast them long-term. Tera Steel allows Breloom to flip its Fairy, Psychic, and Flying weaknesses into resistances, turning the tables on revenge killing attempts from the likes of Gardevoir and Galarian Zapdos, while Tera Normal lets Facade 2HKO the likes of Amoonguss.

Breloom fits best on bulky offense to balanced teams due to its ability to stomach Knock Offs and status while keeping up offensive pressure. Breloom is a great partner for special attackers such as Raikou, Volcanion, and Basculegion-F, all of which can bring it in safely versus special sponges such as Cyclizar and Hisuian Goodra. Breloom also a great teammate for Armarouge, which dispatches bulky Psychic-type Pokemon like Slowbro and Reuniclus while Breloom switches into the plenty of bulky Dark- and Water-type Pokemon like Umbreon and Empoleon that Armarouge might struggle with. Similarly, Slowbro pairs well with Breloom, as it resists Fire- and Psychic-type attacks like Sacred Fire and Psychic Noise from Entei and Reuniclus for it, while Breloom resists Electric- and Dark-type attacks like Thunderbolt from Raikou and Magnezone and Knock Off from Krookodile. Krookodile is also a great partner for Breloom, as it removes Heavy-Duty Boots and Rocky Helmet from foes like Slowbro, Chesnaught, and Hippowdon while also setting up Stealth Rock to chip it's usual checks like Chesnaught. Physical sweepers like Bisharp and Gyarados enjoy Breloom weakening physical walls like Slowbro, Chesnaught, and Hippowdon while absorbing Toxic and Thunder Wave from the likes of Umbreon and the aforementioned Slowbro.

movesets.name: Focus Sash (Fighting)
movesets.description:
Breloom fulfills a variety of roles for Fighting teams, with Spore immobilizing threats like Corviknight, Pelipper, and Toxapex and operates as a revenge killer with Mach Punch. Swords Dance further boosts its great Attack and lets Breloom take advantage of forcing foes out after they have been afflicted with Spore to set up. Bulldoze can be used in place of Spore or Swords Dance to handle Poison-types that would otherwise give it problems like Okidogi and Toxapex. However, Spore and Swords Dance are usually preferred, since the former grants Breloom great utility while the latter can potentially turn it into a setup sweeper. Bullet Seed is a strong STAB move that threatens Ground-types like Clodsire and Great Tusk as well as breaking Ogerpon-C's Sturdy and OHKOing it outright after a Swords Dance boost. Mach Punch, when boosted with Swords Dance, turns Breloom into a setup sweeper, taking on faster threats like Hoopa-U, Kyurem, and Excadrill.

Offensive Great Tusk is one of Breloom's best teammates, as it sets up Stealth Rock to bolster Breloom's breaking and sweeping capabilities, removes entry hazards with Rapid Spin to preserve Breloom's Focus Sash, and handles sun teams thanks to Protosynthesis. In return, Breloom handles Water-types that threaten Great Tusk such as Greninja and Primarina. Keldeo and Urshifu-R not only handle Fire-types like Heatran and Ceruledge, but Keldeo also outpaces and threatens non-Choice Scarf Landorus, while Urshifu-R can revenge kill weakened sweepers and cleaners like Volcarona, Choice Scarf Iron Valiant, and Flutter Mane with Aqua Jet. Choice Scarf Sneasler and Assault Vest Iron Hands make for great teammates, as they handle Fairy-types like Flutter Mane and Enamorus for Breloom thanks to their great special bulk and, in the case of the former, its Poison typing. Additionally, Sneasler can potentially spread status with a combination of Poison Touch and Dire Claw and pivot Breloom in with U-turn, while Iron Hands handles Flying-types like Corviknight, Mandibuzz, and Articuno thanks to its Electric typing. Choice Scarf Iron Valiant, with its colorful coverage, threatens a multitude of pesky threats such as Dragapult, Latios, and physically defensive Gyarados. Lastly, Breloom's wallbreaking enables sweepers like Victory Dance Hisuian Lilligant and Unburden Sneasler to sweep late-game.

movesets.name: Focus Sash (Grass)
movesets.description:
Breloom is a great late-game cleaner for Grass teams by virtue of its great Attack stat, access to Swords Dance to increase it further, and great ability in Technician boosting many of its attacks. Spore allows Breloom to incapacitate a threat to open up opportunities for it to set up Swords Dance. Mach Punch boosted by Technician allows Breloom to not only revenge kill fast cleaners like Meowscarada, Greninja, and Barraskewda but also sweep through teams that lack a check to it like Dark and Ice. Rock Tomb provides great coverage, targeting Fire- and Flying-types that switch in on an anticipated Bullet Seed such as Ogerpon-H, Talonflame, and Zapdos. Close Combat is more powerful than Mach Punch, making it suited for slower foes such as Archaludon, while Bulldoze allows Breloom to handle one of its biggest counters in Gholdengo. Bullet Seed is Breloom's strongest wallbreaking STAB option thanks to Technician boosting each of its hits. A Swords Dance + 3 attacks variant can be used as well to further Breloom's role as a sweeper. However, Spore is preferred, since it helps Breloom find chances to set up.

Breloom appreciates entry hazard support from Toedscruel and Brambleghast wearing down foes, as well as breaking Ogerpon-C's Sturdy so Breloom can immediately OHKO it with Mach Punch. Additionally, the two of them provide entry hazard removal with Rapid Spin so that Breloom's Focus Sash does not break. Amoonguss is a great defensive partner that threatens Fairy-types such as Enamorus and Iron Valiant, and it can also run Spore so that Breloom can choose to run Swords Dance instead. Meowscarada appreciates Breloom immobilizing threats with Spore and removing Toxapex and Ting-Lu, and in return, it handles Ghost- and Psychic types such as Gholdengo, Sinistcha, and Latios. Ogerpon-H and Ogerpon-C appreciate Breloom handling their checks such as Greninja, Barraskewda, and Ogerpon-W for them. In return, Ogerpon-H handles bulky Grass-types such as Sinistcha and Amoonguss, while Ogerpon-C threatens Flying-types such as Articuno and Moltres. Abomasnow sets up Aurora Veil to make Breloom harder to take down, allowing it to find more opportunities to set up and sweep.

movesets.name: Offensive
movesets.description:
• Since it can sleep foes without restriction, Breloom is a monstrous foe that applies serious pressure at Team Preview!

  • Bulldoze: This is Breloom's best option against Gholdengo and provides valuable speed control.

  • Spore: As good as Spore is, it's well prepared for enough by threats such as Gholdengo, Garganacl, and Lum Berry that going without it can make sense.

  • Rock Tomb: Rock Tomb provides a form of speed control that can't be walled by Flying-types like Dragonite.

  • Close Combat: Close Combat lets Breloom muscle past bulkier threats more easily, such as Wo-Chien.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low / Medium: While Breloom can certainly take advantage of Terastallization, Focus Sash variants are used fairly early in the game and often don't need it. Loaded Dice Breloom, however, does like Terastallization covering up its iffy defensive typing.

  • Fire: With Tera Blast, Tera Fire provides an alternative way to get past Gholdengo, avoids getting burned by other foes, and gives bulkier Breloom a chance against Flutter Mane and Focus Sash Chien-Pao.

  • Fighting: Tera Fighting is a good choice for picking off foes more easily with Mach Punch.

  • Grass: Bullet Seed's boost from Tera Grass means it will OHKO Chien-Pao through its Focus Sash if Breloom rolls at least three hits.

  • Rock: Besides boosting Rock Tomb's damage output, Tera Rock prevents Sandstorm from breaking Breloom's Focus Sash.

  • Ground: Tera Ground-boosted Bulldoze has a 93.8% chance to OHKO 4 HP Gholdengo, making Breloom a situational lure. It also severely punishes Rotom-W that attempt to Volt Switch out, and Hippowdon that don't Terastallize.

Items

  • Focus Sash: Since Breloom's bulk isn't very good, Focus Sash is the most reliable way to fire off Spore.

  • Loaded Dice: Guaranteeing 4 hits from Bullet Seed can be quite useful for bulkier Breloom sets, clinching an OHKO on Flutter Mane, Chien-Pao, and Iron Bundle regardless of them running Substitute or Focus Sash.

EV Spreads

  • 4 HP / 252 Atk / 252 Spe: If using Focus Sash, maximizing Speed is important to deal with slower foes that might invest in Speed, such as Corviknight and Skeledirge.

  • 252 HP / 180 Atk / 76 SpD: This bulkier spread makes sense if using Loaded Dice and Swords Dance, letting Breloom survive one hit from Iron Bundle, Chien-Pao, or Choice Specs Flutter Mane with the correct Tera type.

movesets.name: SubSeed
movesets.description:
• With Poison Heal, Breloom can act as a pivot versus defensive Pokemon such as Dondozo and Umbreon as it is unaffected by Yawn.

  • This set can catch opponents expecting the more popular Focus Sash set off guard. However, do note that this set is very susceptible to Taunt and Encore, which can make it difficult to even select Breloom in the team preview phase.

  • Protect: Protect gives Breloom an opportunity to scout out its opponents and further stall them out once Leech Seed has been set up.

  • Timer Stalling: If you obtain a numerical advantage early in the match, you can utilize Breloom to win on timer. This is particularly effective since the Leech Seed damage happens after recovery from Leftovers and Poison Heal.

  • Bulldoze: Bulldoze allows Breloom to further support its teammates and threaten Gholdengo, which likes to absorb status moves. Do be wary that many Gholdengo are Tera Flying, which can render Breloom ineffective versus it.

Other Options
  • Toxic: Toxic can be difficult to fit into the set, but it allows Breloom to punish Tera Grass foes that attempt to circumvent Breloom's Spore and Leech Seed.
Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - High: While Breloom's typing does have some useful resistances, its low bulk means more favorable resistances granted by Terastallization can be key to setting up.

  • Water: This defensive Tera type allows Breloom to resist Baxcalibur's Icicle Spear and Skeledirge's Torch Song, both of which are threats to Substitute. It also helps against Chien-Pao and Chi-Yu, though note that Choice Specs Chi-Yu can still OHKO with Tera Fire Overheat.

  • Fire: This Tera type allows Breloom to resist Ice- and Fire-type attacks while also providing Breloom with a Fairy-type resistance. With Toxic, Breloom is able to fight back against common Grass-type switch-ins. However, this type has more weaknesses when compared to Water.

EV Spreads

  • 252 HP / 252 Def / 4 Spe with Impish: This spread allows for maximum physical bulk.

  • 156 HP / 100 Def / 252 Spe with Jolly: This spread allows for maximum Speed and can survive a Choice Band Extreme Speed from Tera Normal Dragonite after Stealth Rock.

  • 204 HP / 164 Def / 140 Spe with Impish: This spread hits a Speed stat of 108 which ties 4 Spe Adamant Baxcalibur. Furthermore, the defensive investment means that after Terastallization, Breloom's Substitute has a high chance of surviving three hits from Baxcalibur's Icicle Spear.

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 6 onwards

Price Range: 6-7 points

Overview: Breloom may look like quite the fungi, but it's no sleeper when it comes to battle. Its access to the coveted Spore alone is enough to keep any opponent up at night, but its sky-high Attack and Technician-boosted moves like Bullet Seed, Mach Punch, Rock Tomb, and Bulldoze allow it to put foes to sleep the old-fashioned way as well. Even foes capable of walling Breloom are never truly out of the woods: with Poison Heal and moves like Leech Seed, Substitute, and Toxic, it's always capable of turning the tables and making those checks mere setup fodder! Unfortunately, even though Breloom's teambuilder options violate the Geneva Conventions, Breloom itself is held back by the fact that it simply can't run everything it wants to at once; its Poison Heal sets often rely on prediction to be threatening attackers, while Technician sets are quick to get worn out if Breloom it isn't hitting the right moves. Pair that with its saddening Base Stats and the many ways of checking Spore, and you've got a versatile Pokemon with mushroom for improvement, as Breloom can often feel inconsistent when compared to other similarly-priced picks.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Offensive Utility: As a rare offensive Spore user, Breloom has no trouble making openings for itself just by hitting the battlefield, and despite having the bulk of an actual mushroom, access to Poison Heal and resistances to common types like Ground, Dark, and Electric give Breloom several opportunities to get its stubby little claws onto the field. After scaring out any foe not sporting the proper tech, it can get to work while hiding behind a Substitute to thwart its passive would-be checks with Focus Punch and Leech Seed, break through walls with Swords Dance and its massive coverage, or simply spread other status with Toxic.

Wallbreaker: With Breloom's impressive Attack and plethora of Technician-boosted moves, any opponent will find that switching into this thing isn't an easy task, even if Spore is out of the equation. With a Choice Band or Swords Dance boost, Breloom can even act as a cleaner and revenge killer with Mach Punch!

Disruptor: Breloom can invest fully into the sheer menace of Spore, playing with the sole intention of putting a specific target to rest. Whether it's using a Focus Sash to act as a pseudo-stopgap or pushing the limits of its bulk with Poison Heal and investment, if the opponent doesn't respect Breloom, they'll be sleeping with the fishes.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Bullet Seed, Seed Bomb, Mach Punch, Close Combat, Drain Punch, Force Palm, Low Kick

Setup Moves: Swords Dance, Bulk Up

Utility Moves: Spore, Stun Spore, Toxic, Leech Seed, Substitute, Protect, Brick Break

Coverage: Aerial Ace, Bulldoze, Facade, Gunk Shot, Poison Jab, Pounce, Rock Slide, Rock Tomb, Stone Edge, Tera Blast, Thunder Punch, Zen Headbutt

Niche Moves

Focus Punch: Breloom's ability to make foes dance is put on full display when running Focus Punch, letting it score massive damage when predicting switches or behind a Substitute.

Fling: The classic Fling + Big Nugget combo allows Breloom to deal massive damage to bulky Psychic- and Ghost-types that it might otherwise struggle with. Toxic Orb sets aren't out of the fun either; pair that with Fling, and you've got yourself both a one-time Toxic that can bypass Taunt and a newly-found immunity to Poltergeist!

Counter: Counter lets Focus Sash Breloom eliminate desired physical threats, all while avoid the guess-and-check work that comes with potential Spore counterplay.

Common Items

Toxic Orb: Armed with one of the world's finest delicacies: deadly toxins, Breloom can reliably activate Poison Heal and stay healthy.

Choice Band: Technician Breloom's already-deadly ability to break and clean up teams only gets deadlier with the power of a Choice Band. Choice Band sets can even keep Spore to really turn the opponent's hair gray.

Focus Sash: Though Breloom isn't known for bulk, Focus Sash lets it tank any single hit, letting it shut down almost any sweeper with a well-placed Spore or super effective hit.

Damage-boosting Items: With the sheer amount of power and coverage Breloom has at its claws, the damage boosts from an Expert Belt, Life Orb, or Black Belt are never unwanted!

Niche Items

Resistance Berries: Similar to Focus Sash, resistance Berries allow Breloom to take a hit and decommission whatever foe it chooses, even in games where entry hazards and chip damage seem inevitable.

Loaded Dice: Bullet Seed may as well shoot actual bullets when Breloom holds a Loaded Dice; the increase in hits combined with the increased damage with Technician results in a move that can wear out all but the bulkiest checks fast.

Lum Berry: Surprisingly, Breloom sets without Poison Heal don't like getting statused very much. Running Lum Berry lets it avoid those pesky status effects without sacrificing Technician's damage output.

Eject Pack: Bulky Poison-types that prey on Breloom's lack of pivot moves are in for a wake-up call; with an Eject Pack, it's just one Close Combat away from bringing in your team's Poison-type check unscathed.

Tera

Although Breloom's serviceable base typing and unimpressive Speed means it's no paragon of Terastallization, its massive utility and raw firepower make it worth considering as a secondary Tera Captain regardless. Tera Fire and Fighting are among its most common Tera types, with the former offering powerful coverage and the latter boosting its already-strong STAB attacks. On the other hand, Tera Poison, Rock, and Electric boost Breloom's existing coverage moves to new heights while giving it a decent defensive typing, and Tera Steel lets it flip almost all of its defensive matchups in a single turn.

Draft Strategy

The sheer variety of sets Breloom can run means it can find a place in almost any team looking for a strong Fighting-type with a bit of disruptive spice. It's often drafted for Spore, but the nature of that move means it's unwise to expect Breloom to get one off every game. Not that it needs to; just the expectation of Spore alone forces the opponent to play very carefully around Breloom, which a team with these strengths can use to their advantage!

Knock Off: One of the best ways of dealing with Spore counterplay is to remove it entirely; no Safety Goggles are safe from Knock Off users like Roaring Moon and Tinkaton!

Steel-types: Breloom has many ways of dealing with its dedicated checks, but bringing it with a Steel-type partner like Metagross and Gholdengo is one of its simplest tricks. They resist almost all of the types it is weak to, letting them easily take advantage of whatever passive Poison-type it managed to bring in.

Entry Hazard Control: Toxic Orb sets may not particularly care about entry hazard chip damage, but with its poor bulk and Speed, those will be the only sets Breloom can run if it's not paired with a hazard remover like Iron Treads or Blastoise.

Pivots: Any pivot from Iron Moth to Mandibuzz can ensure Breloom gets in without fear of getting picked off with super effective coverage, getting worn out by neutral hits, or just switching into a Knock Off before Toxic Orb has time to activate.

Setup Sweepers / Cleaners: Wincons such as Salamence and Necrozma generally like it when their bulky checks are put to sleep via Spore or simply whittled down from the wallbreaking Breloom provides.

Checks and Counters

Spore Lures: With all of its stats besides Attack leaving a lot to be desired, Breloom can be easy pickings when it's caught by surprise. An unscouted Safety Goggles or sudden Substitute is often enough to shut down a Spore attempt, and if one of these is run on something Breloom isn't expecting, it's getting forced out at best and KOed at worst!

Poison- and Flying-types: Poison-types like Pecharunt and Flying-types like Zapdos resist Breloom's STAB moves and can easily OHKO it it back, both types restricting what sets it can run and making it more prone to clicking a wrong move. Though both types have to watch out for its coverage, Poison-types in particular are excellent candidates for more consistent Breloom checks, as they're immune to Toxic and usually don't mind holding Safety Goggles.

Multi-hit and Sound-based Attacks: Focus Sash and Substitute shenanigans mean nothing to multi-hit attackers like Baxcalibur and sound-based attackers like Kommo-o respectively! Their ability to pressure Breloom even when it's hiding behind these gimmicks is bad news, as with Breloom's poor bulk, they're threatening potential OHKOs.
